title: Define lightweight compatibility tags and runtime-profiling artifacts for open-model intake
creator: Asha Patel
description: Clarify requirements for a lightweight, machine- and human-readable compatibility tagging scheme and a minimal runtime profiling artifact that every new open-model intake must include. Goal is to make onboarding faster for community/open weights while giving runtime and ops teams the required signals for pinning, fallback, and rollout decisions without full model benchmark sweeps.
requirements: Define a small set (<=8) of compatibility tags that cover practical runtime and API constraints (examples below).

Specify a runtime-profiling artifact format (perf.json) that includes nominal token latency at 16/32/1024 seq lengths, peak memory footprint for typical batch sizes (1,4,8), and a flag for KV-cache stability. Artifact must be machine-parseable and human-readable.

Establish acceptance rules for auto-pin recommendations: if perf.json latency and memory fall within verified rails for a target class, recommend 'auto-pin' with suggested variant and quantization profile; otherwise mark 'requires-eval'.
Require an explicit fallback_policy string on catalog entries (e.g., fallback-to: gptx-compat-small) and a canary rollout plan template for hosted and dedicated deployment paths.

Add minimal safety and signature checks: model signature (ONNX/torchscript/transformer architecture marker), license compatibility note, and pointer to a small prompt-eval set (5-10 cases) showing output stability.
Document how tags map to runtime routing decisions and cost/latency trade-offs to be consumed by smart routing and Optimize recommendations.
proposed_solution: Introduce a tag taxonomy: api_compatible, kv_cache_safe, quant_friendly, batchable, long_context_tested, streaming_ok, memory_efficient, known_issues

Specify perf.json schema with fields: model_id, variant, seq_lengths=[16,32,1024], latency_ms_per_token, peak_gpu_mem_mb, batch_sizes=[1,4,8], kv_cache_behavior={stable|unstable|untested}, quant_profiles=[int8,int4], created_by, created_at.
Implement intake pipeline validations: parse perf.json, validate tag presence, run quick smoke inference on a standard small prompt set, and surface failures to the PM/Eng intake gate.
Create an 'auto-pin' heuristic that uses perf.json thresholds and a confidence score; low-confidence cases are flagged for an eng eval ticket.
acceptance_criteria: Tag taxonomy doc reviewed and approved by Runtime and Serving teams (sign-off comment in PRD).
perf.json schema published in the model-catalog README and used by at least one new community-model intake as a dry-run.
Automated intake validation exists and will reject artifacts missing required fields (tags and perf.json) with actionable error messages.
Auto-pin heuristic runs deterministically in the intake CI and produces a recommended_variant string for 80% of dry-run models; remainder produce 'requires-eval'.
Catalog UI wireframe shows tags on model card and exposes fallback_policy; Console team reviews and approves UX copy.
Security and legal confirm that license field and minimum signature checks are sufficient for initial intake (email thread archived).
out_of_scope: Full-benchmark suite for every community model (we only require a lightweight perf.json and a small smoke test).
Automated retraining or fine-tuning as part of intake.
Deep safety evaluations beyond the 5-10 case prompt-eval smoke test.
notes: Trade-offs: smaller tag set reduces onboarding friction but may hide edge-case incompatibilities; we'll iterate tags based on intake failures.
We need an initial pilot with 3 community models (one quant-friendly, one long-context, one streaming) to validate schema and thresholds.
Runtime team prefers machine-parsable perf.json for automated routing; Console team needs human-readable summary for cards — both are satisfied by the same artifact if well-structured.
